These are original Wyreup geometry fixtures released under the repository MIT license. No competitor or parser-library fixture was copied. `stl-cube.stl` is an independently authored, outward-oriented 10 × 10 × 10 mm cube with twelve triangles. `stl-open.stl` is one triangle and is intentionally unsupported. `stl-fixtures.ts` independently encodes explicit box and hollow-box coordinates as ASCII or binary STL; it imports no implementation under test.

Known oracles at layer height 2 mm: cube planes 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 mm, four corners (0,0), (10,0), (10,10), (0,10), area 100 mm², perimeter 40 mm at every layer. The hollow box has the same outer contour and hole corners (3,3), (7,3), (7,7), (3,7), outer area 100, hole area 16, net area 84 mm² and total perimeter 56 mm. Two horizontally separate cubes have area 200 and two loops. Two cubes spanning Z 0–2 and 8–10 have layers 3,5,7 empty. A 1-inch cube uses exact conversion 25.4 mm/in: area 645.16 mm², perimeter 101.6 mm. Translation 99990–100000 in XYZ must yield the same artifact as the origin cube with translation (-99990,-99990,-99990).

Tolerance oracles: moving one face corner by 2.1 epsilon in Z leaves an open edge; moving one corner by (0.3epsilon,0.3epsilon,0) welds within actual Euclidean distance. Only `z > plane + epsilon` is upper; near-plane vertices are on the lower side, and a crossing endpoint within epsilon uses that endpoint's XY at the requested plane. Coplanar triangles skip. Disconnected closed vertex fans at a shared vertex reject as nonmanifold. Binary headers and fixed facet words are ignored non-geometric metadata. Stored normal numbers must be finite even though vertex geometry determines the actual planes; colored facet words carry no color promise.

Tests parse the returned G-code with a separate permitted-command reader and compare every layer and closed loop against these fixed numeric oracles. No geometry is generated with the STL parser/slicer being tested. Browser tests use the same original coordinates and reopen downloaded bytes; browser and package-worker acceptance are separate from pure geometry checks.

The independently authored cube golden artifact is `stl-cube.expected.gcode`. At height 9.999999999999998 mm the prescribed `floor(extentMm*1000+1e-6)` gives five full 2 mm layers; an otherwise tiny negative partial-top remainder clamps to zero, while a positive remainder is retained. A bounded-allocation fixture comprises 626 separated 0.5 × 1 × 100 mm boxes spread along X: at 0.05 mm height its vertical facets exceed 10 million candidate intersections before the packed candidate array is allocated. A separate 200-box layout stresses the spatial-pair sweep and rejects at 2 million checks.

`precisionNotchPrism` is original geometry with a 1.385929e-6 mm short diagonal edge whose two endpoints round to the same six-decimal XY coordinate. It is explicitly unsupported by the current reviewed mesh ambiguity policy: faces2/14 reject during preflight. This is preserved as rejection evidence, not an accepted clean mesh or end-to-end artifact. The formatter-boundary regression instead uses a clearly labelled synthetic strict report, with independently known positive area99.99999mm² and explicit perimeter arithmetic, to reproduce degenerate movement after formatting without claiming that unsupported STL was accepted.
